evidence: data/cts/cts_segments.txt (sha256 117cff6ce5b647b4ee6f5e51040787714441f12e0a0b46eaf8251c3910b4f123) labels the same asset_id as `Champlain Towers South`, so the key is right and the name/type columns are wrong -- the join is not what broke, a column is.

data/cts/cts_asset.json (sha256 fd8986930377530a1f463d365bc090a92cf4205769960b8bee6ed2d4e238ca69) is the site's own asset record: label `Champlain Towers South`, asset_id `null` -- the package never needed an id from the export.

The label is not a cross-reference to a second asset either: Werder's committed meta (data/werder_havel/support/werder_havel_ocv_channels_meta.json) pairs the same string with asset_id 40f420c6-c38e-5eab-8f2b-ac00d66707d0. The CTS rows therefore mix a CTS key with a Werder label.

The defect is upstream: erlking_mvp/tools/ocv_table.py (outside this repository) copies the columns into the support table as `committed_*`. Haltern and Carola carry coherent triples in their own measurement exports, so CTS is the only site affected.

No CTS result reads the columns as identity: the only reference is the passthrough list `SOURCE_TEXT` in code/cts/cts_ocv_core.py; the plates, the DiD layer and the support migration key on `track`/`role`/`day`.
entries.finding: `asset_id` and the `asset_name`/`asset_type` pair do not belong to the same asset: the key is CTS's, the labels are Werder's. No asset in this repository carries this triple.
entries.report_wording: Name the site `Champlain Towers South` from data/cts/cts_asset.json, or by its tracks. Never print the asset_name column as if it described this record.

entries.finding: The column is named like an acquisition-request key but carries the track label: it equals `track` on all 711 rows of the table, so nothing is lost -- only the name is wrong. Read `track`.

At Werder the three columns are internally consistent and agree with data/werder_havel/reference/werder_havel_aoi.json. They are listed here only so that the identical name string in the CTS tables cannot be mistaken for them.

identity_note: `id` is the pipeline row key (`<track>_<date>`); `track` is the footprint and carries the role (`target`, `control_ctn`, ...); `day` is the acquisition day. Together they name a row of every site's table without any asset metadata.
rule: A quarantined column is provenance only. It is copied verbatim from its source and is never used to select, join, group, sort or label a record; identity is `identity_columns`. The records stay byte-identical -- the sha256 of every file named below is pinned here -- so a quarantine changes the reader, not the data. Repairing a source is a separate, documented amendment of the source and of this register, never a silent edit.
